info.name: Microsoft Windows 10 List DirectX graphics devices

items.docs: Enumerates available DirectX graphics adapters using DXGI (DirectX Graphics Infrastructure). Returns information about each adapter including vendor, device ID, dedicated video memory, shared system memory, and feature level support.

info.name: Microsoft Windows 10 Get graphics device details

items.docs: Retrieves detailed information about a specific graphics adapter including supported feature levels, output displays, and hardware capabilities such as shader model support, ray tracing tier, and mesh shader support.

info.name: Microsoft Windows 10 Create a DirectX resource

items.docs: Creates a GPU resource such as a buffer, texture, or render target using ID3D12Device.CreateCommittedResource or similar methods. Resources are allocated in GPU heaps and can be used for vertex buffers, index buffers, constant buffers, textures, and render targets.

info.name: Microsoft Windows 10 Create a command queue

items.docs: Creates a Direct3D 12 command queue (ID3D12CommandQueue) for submitting command lists to the GPU. Command queues can be of type Direct, Compute, or Copy, determining which GPU operations they support.

info.name: Microsoft Windows 10 Create a graphics pipeline state

items.docs: Creates a graphics pipeline state object (ID3D12PipelineState) that defines the complete rendering pipeline configuration including vertex shader, pixel shader, input layout, rasterizer state, blend state, depth stencil state, and render target formats.

info.name: Microsoft Windows 10 Create a swap chain

items.docs: Creates a DXGI swap chain (IDXGISwapChain) for presenting rendered frames to a window or output. The swap chain manages the back buffer(s) and handles presentation including v-sync and frame latency.
